claims.text: Within 10 days of the COVID-19 global pandemic declaration, worldwide mean daily step counts decreased by 5.5% (287 steps).
Within 30 days of the COVID-19 global pandemic declaration, worldwide mean daily step counts decreased by 27.3% (1432 steps).
Italy exhibited a 48.7% maximal decrease in daily step count following its nationwide lockdown.
Sweden exhibited a 6.9% maximal decrease in daily step count while advocating for social distancing without a national lockdown.
Countries with low COVID-19 infection rates that did not institute lockdowns still exhibited decreases in overall step count.

limitations.text: Sampling bias due to reliance on smartphone and app ownership.
Measurement error from smartphone-measured step counts and variability in smartphone carry and use habits.
Lack of assessment of activity intensity and inability to capture nonstepping exercise.
Dataset is a nonrepresentative convenience sample with a variable number of contributing daily users and lacks participant characteristics beyond IP address.

future_work.text: Conduct more formal analytic studies to assess step count trends and social distancing adherence.

methodologies.name: Deidentified smartphone accelerometry step count analysis
methodologies.description: Descriptive study collecting and analyzing deidentified daily step counts via smartphone accelerometers using Apple and Android algorithms among global users of the Argus app.
datasets: Argus smartphone health app user dataset
conditions: Data collected from 19 January to 1 June 2020
Prepandemic baseline defined as regional mean daily steps from 19 January to 11 March 2020
